parts.name: Humeral head articular cartilage
parts.function_note: the larger, more uniformly convex of the two glenohumeral bearing surfaces -- a major reason for the joint's mobility-over-stability tradeoff (a small, shallow glenoid against a large humeral head).
parts.source: Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.

parts.name: Glenoid articular cartilage
parts.function_note: thinner centrally than peripherally, a documented pattern (a horseshoe/crescent of thicker cartilage peripherally) that increases effective concavity/depth beyond the bony glenoid alone.
parts.source: Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.

function: Hyaline cartilage coating the glenohumeral joint's bearing surfaces, providing a low-friction, load-distributing interface and (lacking direct vascular/nerve supply) relying on synovial fluid diffusion for nutrition.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.

parts.name: Distal humeral articular cartilage (trochlea + capitulum)
parts.function_note: covers the pulley-shaped trochlea (articulating with the ulna) and the rounded capitulum (articulating with the radial head), two distinctly-shaped surfaces on one bone.
parts.source: Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.

parts.name: Proximal ulnar articular cartilage (trochlear notch)
parts.function_note: the C-shaped surface gripping the humeral trochlea, providing the elbow's primary hinge stability.
parts.source: Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.

parts.name: Radial head articular cartilage
parts.function_note: articulates with the capitulum superiorly and, via its circumferential rim, with the ulna's radial notch -- letting the radial head both flex/extend and rotate (pronosupination) within the same joint capsule.
parts.source: Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.

parts.name: Femoral head articular cartilage
parts.attachment_or_location: femoral head, excluding the fovea capitis
parts.function_note: thickest over the weight-bearing superior/anterosuperior region, absent at the fovea capitis where the ligamentum teres attaches.
parts.source: Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.

parts.name: Acetabular articular cartilage
parts.function_note: a horseshoe (lunate) shape, not a complete circle -- the acetabular fossa at its center is non-articular, filled with fat and the ligamentum teres rather than cartilage.
parts.source: Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.

parts.name: Patellar articular cartilage
parts.attachment_or_location: posterior surface of patella (odd + lateral + medial facets)
parts.function_note: the thickest articular cartilage anywhere in the human body, consistent with the very high patellofemoral joint reaction forces generated during activities like stair descent and squatting.
parts.source: Shepherd DE, Seedhom BB (1999) 'Thickness of human articular cartilage in joints of the lower limb.' Ann Rheum Dis 58(1):27-34 -- direct thickness measurements across lower-limb joint surfaces, the actual source of the patella's thickest-in-the-body figure (corrected from Sophia Fox et al. 2009, a general cartilage-biology review that never discusses the patella or joint-specific thickness at all -- caught by adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).

parts.name: Femoral trochlear groove articular cartilage
parts.attachment_or_location: trochlear (patellar) groove of anterior distal femur
parts.function_note: its groove depth is a major determinant of patellar tracking stability; a shallow/dysplastic trochlea is a well-documented risk factor for patellar instability.
parts.source: Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.

parts.name: Talar dome articular cartilage
parts.function_note: covers a surface wider anteriorly than posteriorly, contributing to the ankle's characteristic 'screw-home'-like closer-packed stability in dorsiflexion.
parts.source: Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.

parts.name: Tibial plafond articular cartilage
parts.attachment_or_location: distal tibial plafond (+ medial/lateral malleolar facets)
parts.function_note: together with the malleolar facets forms a deep mortise gripping the talar dome -- among the most congruent, and thinnest average cartilage, weight-bearing joints in the body.
parts.source: Sophia Fox AJ, Bedi A, Rodeo SA (2009) 'The basic science of articular cartilage: structure, composition, and function.' Sports Health 1(6):461-468 -- hyaline articular cartilage zonal structure and typical thickness ranges.
